conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling now that your baby has arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—EPDS for short. It’s simply ten questions about your mood and thoughts over the past seven days; it helps us spot anything from the normal “baby blues” to something that might need extra support. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team, and there’s no judgment—just honesty and care. Ready to start?

First question:  
Over the last week, have you still been able to look forward to things the way you normally would, or has that felt harder to do?

Honestly… nothing really feels exciting right now. I used to love catching up with friends or even just going for coffee, but lately even the thought of it feels kind of “meh.” I’ll still do things—like yesterday I took the baby for a walk—but it felt more like I was just pushing myself through the motions.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I can laugh sometimes… like when my husband made that silly face at 3 a.m. while we were both up with the baby. But it feels kind of forced, and the giggles fade fast. Mostly I’m too tired or worried to find much funny.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really… I’ll tell myself, “Hey, tomorrow we’re going to the grocery store and that’s a little outing,” but I can’t feel the spark I used to. Even planning a small visit from my sister feels like one more chore on a long list, not something I’m eager for.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes… almost every day. If the baby won’t settle, I immediately think it’s because I’m doing something wrong or that I’m not reading his cues right. Yesterday I cried because I couldn’t stop him from crying, and I kept replaying it in my head, convinced a “better mom” would have soothed him faster.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

All the time. Even when he’s sleeping peacefully, I’ll suddenly think, “What if he stops breathing?” or I’ll worry the formula isn’t exactly the right temperature and it’ll hurt his stomach. I know in my head it’s probably fine, but the worry just barges in anyway and sits on my chest until I check him—again.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

A few times this week. It’s like a sudden rush—my heart races, I can’t catch my breath, and I’m sure something awful is about to happen, even though nothing’s going on. Last night it hit while I was folding laundry; I had to sit down and grip the couch cushions until the shaking stopped.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes… most days I feel like I’m drowning in small stuff. The dishes pile up, the baby needs feeding, the trash is overflowing, and I just stare at it all wondering how I’ll ever get through. I usually manage to push through, but it feels like I’m barely treading water, and I’m exhausted before I even start.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Several nights this week. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning— replaying every little thing I might’ve done wrong, worrying about the next feed, listening for the tiniest sound from the crib. Even when the baby sleeps a four-hour stretch, I’m still awake, staring at the ceiling until the sun starts to come up.
I have felt sad or miserable

Most of the week, yeah. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling that just lingers—like I’m walking around with a lump in my throat. I’ll see other moms laughing in the park and wonder why I can’t feel that light. Sometimes the sadness hits so suddenly I have to duck into the other room so my toddler doesn’t see me cry.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s been a few times this week. Like yesterday the baby wouldn’t nap and I just sat in the rocker with him on my chest, tears rolling down for no single big reason—just this wave of overwhelm and sadness I couldn’t stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’m exhausted and discouraged, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 23: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
(EPDS-style responses reviewed)

<sym>Endorsed symptoms</sym>  
- Persistent low mood, tearfulness most days  
- Marked anhedonia (minimal enjoyment, tasks feel burdensome)  
- Excessive maternal guilt / self-blame; rumination on perceived failures  
- Near-daily generalized anxiety and situational panic symptoms (racing heart, breathlessness)  
- Sleep disruption secondary to intrusive worry and rumination despite infant sleeping  
- Feeling overwhelmed, “drowning,” difficulty coping with routine demands  

<med>Pattern consistent with</med> probable postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety; meets threshold for further evaluation.

<med>Risk factors</med>  
- Moderate–severe distress, functional impairment  
- No self-harm ideation reported (screen negative on Q10)  
- No protective factors documented here

<med>Recommendation</med>: Continue to formal assessment (EPDS scoring, clinical interview); consider referral for perinatal mental health services.
